titleEn: Supporting children with dyslexia starts with preparing their teachers
titleZh: 支持阅读障碍儿童，要先让教师做好准备
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: A child pauses at a word, tries it, then looks to the teacher for help. Telling the word to the child can get the sentence moving. Working out what to teach so the child can read similar words independently takes a different kind of expertise.
paragraphs.zh: 一个孩子停在一个单词上，试着读它，然后向老师寻求帮助。把这个单词告诉孩子可以让句子移动。想好教什么，让孩子能独立阅读类似的单词，需要一种不同的专业知识。

paragraphs.en: That expertise is especially important for children with dyslexia, which involves persistent difficulties with word reading and spelling. Reading may be inaccurate, slow or effortful, and the pattern varies between children. Recognising dyslexia is only the first step. Helping requires teaching that targets the skills involved, and that depends on teachers understanding how spoken and written language works.
paragraphs.zh: 这种专业知识对于患有阅读障碍的儿童尤其重要，因为这种儿童在单词阅读和拼写方面存在持续的困难。阅读可能不准确、缓慢或费力，而且不同儿童的模式也不同。认识到阅读障碍只是第一步。帮助需要针对所涉及的技能进行教学，而这取决于教师对口语和书面语言如何运作的理解。

paragraphs.en: Research suggests that children at risk of dyslexia benefit most from such high-quality explicit teaching. In this article, we explain what teachers need to know, what we learned from our research, and why it matters for dyslexia.
paragraphs.zh: 研究表明，有阅读障碍风险的儿童从这种高质量的显性教学中受益最大。在本文中，我们解释了教师需要知道什么，我们从研究中学到了什么，以及为什么它对阅读障碍很重要。

paragraphs.en: Research shows that many children with dyslexia struggle to identify or work with sounds in spoken language, which can make learning the relationships between sounds and letters harder. However, their difficulties are not all the same, and one reading attempt cannot determine what teaching they need. This is where expert knowledge matters.
paragraphs.zh: 研究表明，许多有阅读障碍的孩子在口语中很难识别或处理声音，这会使学习声音和字母之间的关系变得更加困难。然而，他们的困难并不都是一样的，一次阅读尝试并不能决定他们需要什么样的教学。这就是专业知识的重要性。

paragraphs.en: Read “reach” and “react” aloud. You probably have little difficulty with either. But how would you explain why the letters “ea” make different sounds in each word? In reach, the letters work together to represent one sound, the long “e” sound. In react, the word’s structure changes how we group the letters: it divides into re + act. The “e” ends the prefix re-, and the a starts act, so they represent separate vowel sounds. A prefix is a meaningful word part added at the beginning of a word. Recognising such parts draws on morphology: knowledge of word structure.
paragraphs.zh: 大声读“reach”和“react”。你可能对这两个词都没有什么困难。但是你怎么解释为什么字母“ea”在每个单词中发出不同的声音呢？在reach中，字母一起代表一个声音，长“e”的声音。在react中，单词的结构改变了我们对字母的组合方式：它分为re + act。“e”以前缀re-结尾，a以act开头，所以它们代表不同的元音。前缀是加在单词开头的有意义的单词部分。识别这些部分需要依靠形态学：单词结构的知识。

paragraphs.en: Now consider a pupil who tries to read react using the “ea” sound from reach. They may be applying a familiar letter–sound relationship without recognising where the word divides. A teacher could check whether the child can read and understand act, then build re + act and explain how the parts combine in pronunciation and meaning. The child would then practise reading the word, with later checks to see whether they could do so independently.
paragraphs.zh: 现在考虑一个学生，他试图用“ea”的声音来阅读反应。他们可能在应用熟悉的字母和声音的关系，而不知道单词在哪里分开。老师可以检查孩子是否能阅读和理解act，然后建立re + act，并解释部分联合收割机如何在发音和意义上结合。孩子然后练习阅读单词，然后再检查他们是否能独立完成。

paragraphs.en: This is why explicit language knowledge matters. The teacher needs to understand how sounds, letters and word structure interact, then use that understanding to interpret the student’s attempt and choose a useful explanation. Teachers need the knowledge and practical skill to decide what to teach next. Being able to read fluently ourselves does not automatically equip us to do that.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是为什么显性语言知识很重要。教师需要了解语音、字母和单词结构是如何相互作用的，然后用这种理解来解释学生的尝试，并选择一个有用的解释。教师需要知识和实践技能来决定下一步教什么。我们自己能够流利地阅读并不能自动让我们做到这一点。

paragraphs.en: In our study of teachers working in the first three years of primary school in Scotland, 122 teachers completed a knowledge assessment. Their weakest area was phonics, decoding and encoding: understanding relationships between letters and sounds and using them to read and spell. On average, they answered 53% of questions in this area correctly. This knowledge helps teachers explicitly teach word reading and spelling, two skills that dyslexia affects.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们对苏格兰小学前三年教师的研究中，122名教师完成了一项知识评估，他们最薄弱的领域是自然发音、解码和编码：理解字母和声音之间的关系，并利用它们来阅读和拼写。平均而言，他们正确回答了53%的这方面的问题。这些知识有助于教师明确地教授单词阅读和拼写，阅读障碍影响的两种技能

paragraphs.en: One teacher from our study captured the uncertainty: “I can identify when readers are struggling but do not yet have the right skills and experience to help them.” They described “feeling deflated and like I’m failing”.
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究中的一位老师抓住了这种不确定性：“我能识别出读者在挣扎，但还没有合适的技能和经验来帮助他们。”他们描述说，“感觉泄气，就像我失败了”。

paragraphs.en: The concern extends beyond Scotland. A 2026 meta-analysis of 143 studies, most conducted in English-speaking countries, identified gaps in teachers’ language and literacy knowledge.
paragraphs.zh: 这种担忧不仅限于苏格兰。2026年，一项对143项研究（大多数在英语国家进行）的元分析发现，教师的语言和识字知识存在差距。

paragraphs.en: Building knowledge and the skill to use it
paragraphs.zh: 积累知识和使用知识的技能

paragraphs.en: Teacher education should make this expertise an explicit part of preparation. Trainees need to understand sound–letter relationships and word structure (morphology) explicitly. They also need to learn how to assess what a child understands and decide what to teach next.
paragraphs.zh: 教师教育应该把这方面的专业知识作为准备工作的一个明确部分。受训者需要明确地理解语音-字母关系和单词结构（形态学）。他们还需要学习如何评估孩子的理解并决定下一步教什么。

paragraphs.en: There is evidence that preparation can build this knowledge. A review of 20 studies of teacher preparation and training found that programmes allowing teachers to apply their learning under expert guidance produced the largest gains in teacher knowledge. It also reported preliminary evidence of benefits for children’s word reading. Knowledge development and supported practice belong together.
paragraphs.zh: 有证据表明，准备可以建立这种知识。一项对20项教师准备和培训研究的回顾发现，允许教师在专家指导下应用他们的学习的方案在教师知识方面产生了最大的收益。它还报告了有利于儿童文字阅读的初步证据。知识发展和辅助实践是相辅相成的。

paragraphs.en: Our study, Book Buddies, offers one example. In this Scottish programme, trainee teachers combined explicit language and literacy coursework with tutoring children in their second year of primary school who needed additional reading support. Over ten weeks, each child received two individual sessions a week. Trainees rehearsed lessons with peers, used assessment to choose a starting point, monitored progress weekly and adjusted lessons with feedback from teacher educators. Before-and-after assessments showed gains in trainees’ literacy knowledge and reported confidence, and in children’s word reading.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究“书友”（Book Buddies）提供了一个例子。在这个苏格兰项目中，实习教师将明确的语言和识字课程与辅导小学二年级需要额外阅读支持的孩子结合起来。在十周的时间里，每个孩子每周接受两次单独的课程。实习教师与同龄人一起排练课程，通过评估选择起点，每周监测进展情况，并根据教师教育者的反馈调整课程。前后评估显示，受训者的识字知识和报告的信心以及儿童的文字阅读都有所提高。

paragraphs.en: For teachers already working in schools, continuing professional development should address any gaps in the knowledge and practical skills they need. Schools and local authorities can provide this support through targeted continuing professional development, with dedicated time to review pupils’ work, rehearse explanations and receive feedback, as set out in Education Endowment Foundation guidance. Teachers should not have to acquire this expertise by chance.
paragraphs.zh: 对于已经在学校工作的教师，持续专业发展应该解决他们所需的知识和实践技能方面的任何差距。学校和地方当局可以通过有针对性的持续专业发展提供这种支持，按照教育捐赠基金会指南的规定，专门花时间审查学生的作业，排练解释和接受反馈。教师不应该偶然获得这种专业知识。

paragraphs.en: Universities, school leaders and local authorities share responsibility for providing knowledgeable mentors, dedicated time and suitable resources. Confidence should grow from supported experience, while success should be judged through changes in teaching and pupils’ progress.
paragraphs.zh: 大学、学校领导和地方当局都有责任提供知识渊博的导师、专门的时间和适当的资源。信心应该从支持的经验中增长，而成功应该通过教学的变化和学生的进步来判断。

paragraphs.en: The teacher who felt they were failing had already recognised a child’s difficulty. They needed better preparation to know how to respond. When a child struggles to read and looks to their teacher for help, that teacher should have the knowledge and practical skills to turn the moment into an opportunity for learning.
paragraphs.zh: 感到失败的老师已经意识到孩子的困难。他们需要更好的准备，知道如何应对。当孩子阅读困难并向老师寻求帮助时，老师应该拥有知识和实践技能，将这一时刻转化为学习的机会。
